entry.title: A Short Week
entry.content:
This week, I forgot to make copious photos. Almost all of the pictures and all of the gifs in this blog are therefore found using DuckDuckGo; I shall see if I can again make some more photos for next time. Anyways:

Breaking News: On wednesday, I had had enough of my plank of a mattress and I decided to go do something about it. I had plans to get dinner with Martin, a colleague from work. I told Martin of this plan, and he basically told me the equivalent of “Say no more, you need to go to IKEA.”

And so we did. We first feasted scrumptiously at the Hawkers at the Alexandra Village Food Centre, where I established that indeed: the Thai kitchen is so far one of my favourite kitchens in Singapore, and Thai green curry is delicious. I need to get a recipe. Sadly, I am not allowed to cook in my apartment.

Something that caught my eye at the Hawkers was a stall with European style food, which included the exotic dish Chicken with Rice. In fact, as far as I saw it, most of the menu consisted of rice dishes, which amused me. Consider my surprise when it turns out that not only is the IKEA a bona fide restaurant here, but it actually has very European style dishes. I will check this out in the future.

After a bit of a justified splurge in the IKEA and a decidedly uncomfortable busride home, I overhauled my bed. Suffice to say that I have rediscovered sleep, and even though it still takes me two hours to fall asleep these days (lingering jetlag?) I feel better than I have felt for a while.

Other than that, this week was somewhat tame comparing to the past week. My Employment Pass arrived on Friday. Furthermore, My Singtel e-Sim got activated. Like a baffled tourist asshole, I then returned to the store and bothered the overworked Singtel staff with two issues which turned out non-issues:

  1. My Settings showed 2GB of data only, but that turned out to be the warning and just meant the amount of GBs I had to spend before my phone would warn me of data spending had reset.
  2. My phone is simply to geriatric for Singaporean 5G.

As my phone is only three years old, the second one baffles me and I decided to just deal with 4G instead. I did look into maybe getting a phone with my subscription (pending…), but in the end that requires a two year subscription, so to hell with it. Imma call this obsoleteness policy what it is: a waste of perfectly good, if older, smartphones.

(Small update: It has since been pointed out to me by Christiaan that another possible reason my phone does not support Singaporean 5G is because Singapore 5G may function differently from European 5G. This is a very good point, so my annoyance at not having Singapore 5G has significantly reduced. I am still not buying a new phone just to get 5G, however. In fact, it has become less likely that I will buy a phone here within the next year.

This leads to Singapore Lesson 3: Investigate phone frequency bands before you buy a Singapore sim card. Generally a good travel tip.)

I’m pretty embarrassed about going a bit Karen on this, though; I could have easily figured out the first point out if I had given it some more critical thought. It does mean however that all the bureaucratic stuff is done, as far as I know. At least, on the Singapore side…

On the hobby side, I have spent most of my week working on my DnD setting and a campaign module I am working on. For those in the know, it’s based on an earlier campaign I ran, the Fenusia campaign. I am still quite fond of that campaign, but it was flawed, and it eventually ended unfinished.

Where the original campaign started as a sea exploration campaign which eventually became a conspiracy campaign, I am reimagining it as a campaign which balances the sea-exploration and the conspiracy aspects by essentially being a hexcrawl campaign which switches between raising money for expeditions (interacting with the city and its conspiracies) and actually crawling the hexes on a boat (sea-exploration). I also added a new focus on curses, to add in more spooky elements. The campaign will be from level 1 to level 11.

Currently, I have a good setup for the player paths of the campaign and I am redesigning the city of Fenusia (partly based on Venice), including the events that happen in the city during the campaign. These events and the design of the city will then be used to create questlines for the party to make money off of for their expeditions, through which the party can also affect the city.

During initial stages of design, I used a bit of ChatGPT to rubber duck some of my ideas, as almost everyone I play DnD with is also somehow involved in the setting and I did not want to give them spoilers, but I also like to discuss ideas in some manner. ChatGPT is however somewhat limited in this respect (for one, its a yes-man, which I do not need) and it doesn’t replace discussing this stuff with actual people, I caved this week and asked two friends to do some proofreading and to help me along a little.

I am also still learning Frama-C at work. For anyone learning Frama-C, I recommend the tutorial by Allan Blanchard, which I am quite enjoying so far. I did run into some trouble with getting Frama-C to list CVC5 as a Prover, but maybe this will be solved tomorrow. In other work news, I got some more tasks, which I find quite exciting.

As the last tidbits; I started the Librarian movies (and series), I have managed to get a rudimentary audio-microphone setup going, and I have been invited to a boardgame night with the neighbours. Looking forward to that! Also, I heard from both Erfan and Yusuf (another colleague) that the tax situation here is probably even be better than I initially estimated, so I should be a responsible lad and save up more money.

Tomorrow, the quest for the Steam Deck begins!

For now, however, I have been making this blog for around four hours. This means that I have improved my picture game:

This also means, however, that I have not yet managed to fulfill my intention of going to bed around 22:00, which will surely allow me to be asleep roughly at 0:00. As it is now reaching 0:00, I think it is high time I go to bed.

Tom out.

Practical Note: I have not yet been able to look into a mail button, but I have been recommended Twine and/or Feeder as apps to be able to read RSS feeds, including the RSS feed of this site. I will probably eventually look into this, but I make no hard guarantees.

Small update: I have also been recommended Capy Reader as a good app, which has a fantastic logo. Thanks Jore!

This week I have mostly been prepping D&D, so I haven’t consumed much media at all. Instead, I’ll recommend the EP Empire of the Clouds, which is quite nice and calm. I see that one can embed Spotify on sites; let’s see if that works.

entry.title: First Week of Work
entry.content:
Well, that’s my first week of work done. And wouldn’t you know it: immediate long weekend! Turns out that Singapore turns 61; clearly, this means that in about 4 to 8 years, Singapore is eligible for retirement. Somehow, that seems unlikely to happen, but I will be following Singapore’s life choices with great interest.

Stupid jokes aside, I was pretty happy with that extra day of rest; I am still acclimatizing, and this gave me an extra day in which I could focus on living in Singapore and not also at the same time getting myself up to speed with work.

Turns out it was needed, I spent most Saturday reading in bed and playing and learning chess with and from Patrick. I am not particularly good at it, but I think I can see the shape of good chess play now, and perhaps I will get better soon. I am considering to get the Chess app for a year too; might be a fun skill to learn.

So, on work: I have, by now, truly met four people of the group and spoken to another few members. The social element of being part of a research group is far less pronounced than it was at the TU/e, which is something to get used to. However, the group seems to be on top of things with regards to research, and I am confident that I can learn a lot here; now it is up to me to find something I can add to the group’s efforts.

Furthermore, I estimate that I will be able to enjoy working with at least those I have met, and our lunches together so far have been fun and relaxing. Thank you Eduardo for letting Martin know I was going to Singapore. I have an ambition to see how many of the group I can get to join me for lunch, but I have been reliably informed that getting everyone to join a lunch at some point is unlikely to succeed. This will, of course, not stop me for now.

This week, I spent familiarizing myself with the details of C using the book Modern C (thanks Ferry!) and the basics of Frama-C, using a book and the website. C so far is frustrating to me, due to its continued inclusion of historical design choices due to the fact that C is an older language (like the difference between strings and char arrays). The book also has some conventions about programming in C for which the rationale is basically “Just accept this, historically it was done like this.” As someone who has, since his PhD, been focusing on recultivating his curiosity and considers that to be an absolutely bogus reason for the existence of conventions, this does not endear the language to me. Maybe at some point I shall make a little post about my experiences in C programming and analyzing.

On the bureaucratic side, the end of the tunnel is visible. I now have a Singpass, and my Employee Pass (visa) will arrive at the university next week. My address was not correctly communicated to the Ministry of Manpower; this was not debilitating but it sent me on a little sidequest to get that fixed, which ended today when the landlord gave permission for an Employee Pass to be registered at my current address. Furthermore, my bank account works and I have been able to pay all my renting obligations. This did not stop the company from which I rent to send me an invoice the day after I paid the obligations. I tried to contact them through four to six different channels, from which I learnt the following lesson:

Singapore Lesson 2: No news is good news. Do not expect to get confirmation mails for contacting services.

I also had some problems with 2FA authentication; this I had to fix by reinstalling Windows Authenticator, which conveniently defenestrated my 2FA authentication for the TU/e, to which I think I will still have access until February, and to which I more importantly would like to keep access until February as I am the corresponding author for at least some of the AuDaLa papers. I have contacted the TU/e, but they can only reset my 2FA through a meeting, which I will pick back up when my phone issues are done.

Phone-wise, with my Singpass, I can officially register my phone number. Of course, this could not be done through the app, because it turns out Singpass has some trouble communicating one’s nationality to other services when one is Dutch, so today, I visited two different locations of the Singtel phone company to get my phone registered to me.

This should be processed on Wednesday, after which I can transfer my phone to eSim, after which I should try to call the employee of the phone company to check whether I can place outgoing calls, which I for some arcane reason am not able to do (this seems to not be the standard). Then, I should call the phone company for 5G access (I should already have it, but I don’t).

Other than that, I have had dinner with Erfan, as evidenced by the photo’s above. We found evidence of Dutch Presence in Singapore, as well as an English-styled bar where one can order Guinness. Furthermore, I also had dinner with Martin (no photo’s I’m afraid), and tried out pizza from a pizza place in Singapore; the pizza I had some interesting toppings, including chicken, onion, pineapple and crab. Crab really was the mystery ingredient there, as I had no clue it was on the pizza and I spent most of my meal trying to figure out what on earth it was. I had settled on fish, but crab makes sense. Luckily, there is also a pizza place nearby that seems (I make no promises) to sell more italian-style pizza. If I ever want to spend around 20 euro’s for a pizza (which will most likely eventually happen), I will try it out.

Another of my food exploits was the Tasting of the Bread:

I concluded the following:

  1. I am still not a selfie person.
  2. The bread is good, but I doubt I’m gonna find my favourite types of bread here.
  3. Do not eat a full bread without water at hand, it will not feel nice.

In other news: peanut butter is surprisingly not terrible here, but biscuit spread (and some drinks) are sweet enough to rot your teeth where you stand. I also think my toothpaste has an impact on my taste for some reason.

Yesterday, me and a friendly co-worker, David, went to see the fireworks for Singapore’s 61th birthday yesterday, which was fun. I saw some pretty great sights, of which I have photos:

Before me and David went to see the sights as shown above, I decided this was a good opportunity to figure out where to buy a Steam Deck. Luckily for me, there was a gamestore very close at hand, so I went there and asked where I could buy a Steam Deck. So I went to an employee, and he told me that that very store sold steam decks, gesturing downwards:

This was a very sudden end to my side-quest, and as they did not have them in stock right away and I still needed to wait for payday, I could do nothing else than say:

It has been an interesting week. I have noticed that I am still conceptualizing this adventure as a short-term temporary thing, but I am slowly realizing that this is going to be for at least a year, and a year is a long time. This has for now led me to the conclusion that I do not want to miss two years of Poekie’s life, so if I stay for longer Poekie will have to come here. Secondly, I acclimatize reasonably well to moving abroad. I mean sure, I have given an exposition on all the trouble it has been so far, but I find I don’t truly feel like the trouble was a massive imposition; at the moment, it is an amusing annoyance. This also means that it is easy for me to fall into old patterns, which can be a boon or a detriment. I shall have to see.

Well, that’s it for today, I think. I think my next post will be next week. Let’s see if the bureaucratic stuff is truly done then. I’ve also been working on prepping a D&D campaign, maybe I can talk some about that (without spoiling anything). Furthermore, my laptop screen has been glitching a bit; future side-quest? We shall know next week.

(Update: Nevermind, immediately found a fix online. Let’s see if it sticks.)

Tom out.

This weeks media recommendation: Doctor Who, Dalek Universe, a fast-paced 9-episode audio drama saga of the 10th Doctor (around the series 4 specials) traveling to before the Time War, with a focus on the Dalek extended universe as envisioned in Classic Who by for example Terry Nation. Excellent action and character work. I have relistened the first seven episodes, and I have once again been enjoying it quite a lot. Also the sixth episode has some Tolkien parallels, so once again Tolkien did it first, like he invented horses and dwarves. I think I’ll continue with reading the Hobbit soon.

Note that this series has some prerequisites. For starters, it may be beneficial to have seen Doctor Who.

entry.title: Arranging Life in Singapore
entry.content:
I am now at the end of my first week of living in Singapore (sort of, one day late), and I am almost settled.

The good news: I have found a room! The room is nice and spacy, though the furniture is a bit basic and the Wifi does not work yet. The airco works, which is a massive relief, and the view is pretty great, as can be seen on the right.

Furthermore, the location is fantastic; work is a 30 minutes walk, and the busstop is less than 5 minutes walk. There is also a mall reachable in 10-15 minutes, and a bigger mall reachable in 40 minutes. Within a radius of 20 minutes, there are also multiple spots to eat.

The bad news: I have not yet been able to pay for the room. It turns out that getting a functional bank account, for which I had to have a residential address (the room), requires about 2 weeks of working days, first to approve the application and then to issue a debit card. Luckily for me the landlord and agent (three hurrahs for the agent) seem to be fine with me being delayed in paying my first month of rent, otherwise this could have gotten quite nasty. (They highly preferred me using PayNow to pay them as opposed to transferring the payment from the Rabobank.)

The absolute knockout blow from the mace of bureaucracy in which I found that out was pretty magnificent. There I was, sitting behind my work desk on Friday, when I suddenly receive three mails from the bank. Paraphrased (though the order is correct):

Mail 1: “Dear sir, your request to update your e-mail address has been completed.”

Mail 2: “Dear sir, welcome to our bank and welcome to digibanking! Login to generate a digital token! Do not tell your login details or your one-time password to anyone.”

Mail 3: “Dear sir, your debit card has been issued; it will be sent to your address in 3-5 working days.”

Tom:

Like an unbureaucratic fool, I could not see the beautiful perfectly sensible logic at play here; I had already waited for three working days for the application to be approved, so I didn’t expect to have to wait even longer for the debit card. I had also never received login information for digibanking, which according to the mail, I should never share with anyone. I checked the digibanking app: I could make new login information, of course, using five different methods (including using the debit card), none of which were available to me.

So I went to the bank twice that day, standing in no less than 4 lines in total before being plucked out of the last line near closing time and being helped by some lovely bank staff, who explained to me that the idea was that I could access digibanking after I received my debit card.

I can never tell whether it is just me in these situations, but I was again in my baffled tourist state at that point. Got a lovely tip to try out some mango-cheese smoothie at a store called Heytea though; forgot to ask the name of the guy who gave me the tip before I was plucked from that waiting line.

Luckily the bank teller was able to assist me in unlocking digibanking early; the next Friday was decisively after the deadline for paying the first month of rent for the room to such an extent that I was uncomfortable waiting until then. I still need to wait up to three working days to transfer the money required to do that to my Singapore bank though.

Smarter people than me may realize that maybe this could have been avoided through the application of a service like Wise or similar (as was recommended to me by Jagruth and Nikhil from St Jozef Doelen), but I remembered too late and decided to just go with this instead of complicating this situation further.

Am I done then? Not quite, as my employee pass appointment is on Wednesday, after which I have to give proof of Employee Pass to both the phone company and the landlord. Shouldn’t be too difficult, however.

And then, it will all have worked out. All that rests me for now is telling you the definite order of how to arrange things when you go to Singapore:

  1. Get a prepaid simcard. This cannot be an e-Sim; I checked.
  2. Get a proof of ownership for your prepaid simcard.
  3. Get a residential apartment/room/house/registered cardboard box/etc. Make sure that you can pay for this in some way preferably involving access to PayNow, Singapore’s fast payment system, but without requiring access to a specifically Singaporean bank account. Make sure to communicate with your agent and landlord, and remember that at least the Rabobank has a transfer time.
  4. Get an employment pass via work.
  5. When you have a residential apartment and, preferably, a Singpass, make a bank account. Do not make my mistake.

Furthermore: Arrange hotel bookings in intervals of one week, so that you can still cancel the unnecessary bookings. Trust me on that, this is probably the only real mistake I made.

There, done. Super easy, barely an inconvenience.

.

.

.

It turns out I have been in action mode a lot, so I am unsure what to do next, really. Probably work. My first workday was last friday; it was a bit hectic, as I had to go to the bank twice. There was a meeting on what the project was about; it sounds very cool, and it also sounds like I am going to have to become familiar with a lot of different systems in a short timespan. But then, that was expected. It turned out my NUS-id and password did not work yet, and my employee pass request was sent in a bit late, but that should be resolved by Monday and it’s not like I wasn’t running around between different bank branches anyways.

In a surprising twist, I shall first be familiarizing myself with Frama-C, which I first heard about from Bob not even two weeks ago. You can bet that I now regret leaving my Modern C book behind in the Netherlands. Nevertheless, I will still be installing Rocq on this laptop and work through it; I actually quite enjoyed the first bits of Volume 1 of Software Foundations which I worked through before I had to start arranging my move.

On the hobby end, I went to see Spider-Man: Brand New Day. It was good. It had quite some connections to the wider MCU, but it was a movie focused on Spider-Man first and foremost, setting the stage for a new era of MCU Spider-Man. If you like the MCU Spider-Man movies, give it a watch.

Furthermore, me and Erfan have eaten together a few times. He pointed out some good nearby restaurants, which we have been visiting. Here is a photo of us yesterday, sitting in a thai restaurant: Also dear god peppers are spicy here. I already burnt the inside of my mouth quite a bit with some noodles last Sunday and I suffered yesterday when eating a standard red pepper. Erfan told me some more about visiting Malaysia, and it definitely sounds like something I should do (probably with Bram, when he visits).

Next week, I will probably continue with the process of getting all the right documentation and paying for my apartment, as well as do work. I hope to find a way to watch the new Avatar movie, but I currently don’t have wifi, so let’s see whether that works out. I also think I should put some more time into the Discordia stuff, or do some sporting or something. For discordia, I put Krita on my laptop, so I should be able to draw stuff again.

I think I’ll just take it easy the rest of the weekend though. Not like I haven’t been busy a lot recently. Time for a walk.

Tom out.

Note: I have received some nice ideas for functionality on this site, but as I currently do not have wifi, me augmenting the site will have to wait until I do. Thanks for the ideas, though, and if you have another idea, please let me know.

Bonus: I have some additional photos! Two were made before my plane flight (featuring my mom and dad, and one featuring Joep), and one was made by Erfan yesterday. I also added a photo of me in fancy dress for my defense with Poekie.

Bonus reading tip: If you like reading about my bureaucratic misadventures, you can certainly not go wrong with Franz Kafka’s The Trial. I remember reading this one winter’s evening while on my way to Amsterdam. I was so engrossed in it that when I got off the train, the cold of the platform, the sudden throngs of people and the fact that I suddenly did not find myself in a space that could be mistaken for the labyrinthine attic-like hallways that Joseph K. needed to navigate reduced me to the state of a baffled tourist. I remember only snapping out of it a few streets further, before which my body navigated to where I needed/wanted to be (a bookshop, in this case) while my brain frantically tried to get back to reality.

entry.title: Arrival in Singapore
entry.content:
I am in Singapore and I am alive! I was looking for a nice picture to illustrate this victory, preferably one with a derpy cat with two paws in the air, but all pictures I could find looked somewhat fake, so I am going to instead post this delightful picture I got from Mark recently:

I can certainly empathize with the bunny’s victory.

Life in the Singapore housing market goes fast. While still stumbling around like a baffled tourist (a state pretty familiar to me when I don’t have enough sleep), I got a call from an agent I had been communicating with for a room, which happened to be available. I went with the flow, and saw the room, after which the agent was so kind as to join me on the bus towards a phone shop (I hadn’t bought a simcard yet), giving me a good description of the neighbourhood and helping me find some important shops and giving me some handy tips on malls and the MRT.

I think everything would have gone far less smoothly if she hadn’t done that, so I am grateful.

I also got the valuable tip to perhaps visit Malacca in Malaysia at some point; it turns out to also have been a Dutch colony.

With a phone number arranged and a room in the cross-hairs, I then had to get a bank account. Sadly by then (after some sleeping) it was Sunday, and on Sunday, the banks are closed. The Singapore housing market goes fast, however, and this delay was not great for the room: a challenger appeared around the afternoon, and the agent worked tooth and nail to stop the room from being rented out to that challenger.

My hope was that with a bank account, I could pay the good-faith deposit conventional in the Singapore housing market more easily than using the worldwide transfers from the Rabobank, which I had never used before. (The good-faith deposit signifies the intent of the would-be-renter to rent the room, and is transformed into the security deposit after the renting contract is signed.) Sadly, it turns out that like so many things in Singapore, a residential address is needed for a bank account. So that was a wasted day; apologies to the agent.

Therefore, if you ever go to Singapore with an In-Principle-Approval letter for a job as a Research Fellow at the NUS:

  1. Get a prepaid simcard. This cannot be an e-Sim; I checked.
  2. Get a proof of ownership for your prepaid simcard.
  3. Get a residential apartment/room/house/registered cardboard box/etc.
  4. Get a bank account. This requires proof of residential address.

Future steps will still have to be added; my residential address will have to be communicated to the NUS, who will use that for transforming my IPA into a full Employee Pass. With this I can get a Singpass, which I can then use to put a subscription on my sim, and most importantly, to finally be able to check the balance of my public transport card via my phone. I cannot wait.

The public transport is worth every penny here; the MRT (metro/subway) is great, and the buses are also very good. The weather is heavy and damp, but I find that I don’t have as much trouble with it as I expected. I truly am a warmth-enjoyer. I did get a bit of a cold from the air-conditioning, but I will get used to that in time.

This did not stop me meeting up with Erfan, a friend of Nazanin who I had contact with before coming here, and the both of us and Erfan’s dog Bo having a pretty great walk from the shore through the NUS.

I am currently waiting for a contract for renting the room; I hope that will all work out. Jetlag hit me hard tonight; I shocked awake at 2 AM and couldn’t properly sleep after, so I am taking it easy otherwise today. I thought I had avoided jetlag. Jetlag seems to have had other plans.

There is also a high likelihood of me going to the new Spider-Man on Thursday; before that I will probably rewatch Spider-Man No Way Home, as I had a good conversation with Daniel recently that led me to consider giving that one another shot (I didn’t like the amount of nostalgia in it when I first saw it).

And now I shall get back to waiting, probably eating something, and watching a movie. The landlord of the room is now supposed to contact me.

Tom out.

entry.title: First Post!
entry.content:
Today, on Sunday, 19 July 2026, the entity known as Tom Franken somehow stumbled into the internet. It is said he cleaned his glasses at least thrice before he tried his first foray into styling his site, trying to make the icons fit his social media. These icons, however, had other plans, which eventually led to the First Great Icon War of Tom’s site. The war ended in a stalemate, with the X-icon falling to Tom’s brute force methods but Tom being unable to add in a decent mail icon using those same methods. Until further news is heard, it can be assumed that Tom’s journey to refamiliarize himself with web design is still ongoing.

RIP , we barely knew ye.
